title: VOLO BG3 masterlist
description: Load order data for Baldur's Gate 3, mined from load orders players submitted. Published under CC0-1.0: take it, fork it, build on it. The file declared this schema from the start and the schema did not exist, which is a poor welcome for anyone trying to consume the data.

version.description: Schema version of this artefact, not the game or the tool.

generator.description: The script that wrote it. Nothing here is hand-edited.

license.description: SPDX identifier for the mined data. The mod names inside it belong to their authors and Astra's dividers are separate; see notice.

licenseUrl.description: Canonical text of the licence named above.

creator.description: Who to attribute the mined data to.

source.description: Where this file is published and can be re-fetched.

notice.description: Licensing map and third party material, including what CC0 does not cover.

gameBuild.description: Newest base-game build seen in the corpus, e.g. 4.8.700.7143220.

incompatible.description: Mods that must not be installed together. Hand-written only: two mods appearing in an order that broke is not evidence they conflict.

mods.description: Names or UUIDs. Two or more present together triggers the warning.

provenance.description: How much evidence stands behind this build of the masterlist.

working.description: Orders someone reported playing without load order problems. Only these teach sequence.

groups.description: Categories and the order relation between them, the way LOOT models groups.

requirementSatisfiedBy.description: Requirements another mod can meet instead, keyed by the required mod's uuid, valued by the uuids of mods that stand in for it. Hand-written in curated-rules.json: two mods doing the same job share no name, author or metadata, so nothing in the data can find this.

requirementAliases.description: Names a requirement may use for a mod that none of the mod's own strings match, mapped to that mod's uuid. Keyed by lowercased alphanumeric name. Hand-written in curated-rules.json: nothing measurable joins a mod page's title to a differently named pak, and matching on resemblance would invent links between unrelated mods.

name.description: Exactly as the author wrote it. Never normalised: the name is matched against what a user has installed, so tidying it breaks the match.

uuid.description: BG3's own identifier for the mod, lower-cased. Not always a UUID: where no submitted order ever supplied one, this is a synthetic key of the form 'name:<lowercased alphanumeric name>'. That is a second identity namespace, which is why the field is typed as a plain string rather than as a UUID. A consumer joining on this field should expect both shapes and must not parse it as a UUID.

divider.description: Position on Astra's Load Order Dividers, 0 to 105, with fractions for sub-dividers such as 58.11 for a Warlock subclass. The skeleton applies whether or not the divider paks are installed.

oftenAbsent.description: Most working orders declaring this as a requirement do not have it installed, so its absence is reported as a warning rather than as something the load order is broken without. Measured from the corpus, never hand-set. A real library scores zero here.

loadsAfterDependents.description: This mod is loaded after the mods that require it, so its dependencies stop being ordering constraints. Set only where the working orders say so, and only with pooled evidence across several dependants. A patcher reads the mods it patches, so 'requires X' does not mean 'X loads first' for it.

dependencies.description: Declared in the mod's own metadata. Hard constraints on order, and never violated by a group or divider decision, unless the depended-on mod is marked loadsAfterDependents. The requirement itself always stands: a missing dependency is reported either way.

messages.description: Curated warnings, shown whenever the mod is present.

evidence.description: How the category was decided and how much weight it carries. Kept separate so consumers can trust the tiers differently rather than treating a guess as a fact.

source.description: curated is hand-written and outranks everything. section comes from a header a modder wrote. external-category is the mod's own Nexus or mod.io listing. author-catalogue places a mod with its author's other catalogued work. inferred is a vote by neighbouring mods. none means uncategorised, and the mod sorts to the end.

confidence.description: For inferred entries, neighbour agreement from 0.7 to 1.

voloSortedInstalls.description: Of installs, the orders VOLO sorted. Their presence counts, since the mods were really installed and played; their sequence never does, because it is VOLO own answer returning.

alternateNames.description: Other names this mod has been published under, most frequent first. A rename leaves everyone who has not updated listing the old name, so both are in the corpus; these resolve a name nothing else answers to, and never displace a canonical name.

loadAfter.description: Mods this one loads after because an author published a sequence saying so. An ordering, not a requirement: a published load order says these load in this order and does not say the later ones need the earlier ones, so nothing derived from this may report a mod as missing.

plugins.description: One row per mod. uuid is unique across this array and is the key every consumer should join on. JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by property, so the guarantee is stated here and enforced by scripts/smoke-test.mjs rather than by validation. Consumers that break ties themselves have been seen to break them in opposite directions, which is why the constraint is written down.
